key_insight: At affordable mesh resolution, a single phase-field parameter set cannot simultaneously match elastic slope, peak force, and crack path in brittle chocolate fracture.
engineering_relevance: Reliable fracture predictions for food processing and handling require calibration to a declared objective, with numerical settings and boundary conditions reported.
method: Compare sharp-interface and diffuse phase-field frameworks for Griffith-type fracture in cooled dark chocolate.
Identify elastic parameters from pre-crack tension and compression, then critical energy release rate from three-point-bending peak force.
Calibrate phase-field width last, accounting for mesh-resolution constraints.
evidence_signal: The assessment uses tension, compression, and three-point bending to examine parameter calibration, while evaluating how phase-field width affects structural response, crack curvature, and stress fields.
watch_item: Mesh-limited phase-field width can alter predicted fracture behavior, so calibration must target a specified observable rather than assume simultaneous agreement across all outputs.
paper_title: Finite Element Modeling of Fracture in Brittle Foods with Physically Consistent Parameter Calibration: A Practical Case Study on Cooled Dark Chocolate
